text:
s2arm.com 

 [!NOTE]
 Good news: s2arm.com is now the official S2Arm website. S2Arm is free and open source and never accepts donations; get S2Arm only from s2arm.com or this GitHub repository.

 Your own Switch games, running natively on iPhone, iPad and Mac. Game code is rewritten to native ARM64 and runs directly on the device's processor, with graphics going straight to Metal. Your whole library lives in one app, and a few clicks in the Mac or Windows launcher take a game from import to play.

Platforms: iPhone / iPad (iOS / iPadOS 18 and later) · Mac (Apple silicon, macOS 15 and later) · Build on Mac or Windows · Android / HarmonyOS coming soon · License: Apache-2.0 · Bring your own games 

简体中文 · Download the launcher · All releases · Evidence

 

 A native port, not an emulator

The game's own ARM64 code is rewritten at build time and then runs directly on the processor in your iPhone, iPad or Mac. There is no CPU emulator in between. Graphics calls are translated straight to Metal, and system services come from a native host. That is where the speed, the low heat and the battery life come from. Evidence

 One app, your whole library

Every game you import goes into the same S2Arm app; open it and pick what to play. The whole library takes a single App slot on your developer account, so adding a game never means installing another app or spending another signing slot. Evidence

 Graphical launchers, next to zero setup

There is a graphical launcher for Mac and one for Windows. On first launch the welcome page boils everything down to three steps: get this computer ready, add your keys, add your games, with a single primary button at any moment. Everything else is either bundled or fetched in one click, and you never touch a command line.

After you click Build, every stage shows its progress, elapsed and remaining time, and disk use. Several games can queue up and build one after another. Evidence

 
 
 
 

 
 
 
 

 Let an AI drive

Both the Mac and Windows launchers expose a control interface, s2armctl . An AI assistant can import games, build, install, follow progress and read errors, and every step shows up in the launcher window. A companion self-check, self-fix and feedback toolkit lets the AI find a problem, apply the documented fix, and, when it cannot, package a diagnostic bundle for you to file. Watch an AI diagnose and fix a real problem end to end: Evidence

 Have an AI do it for you

Send this to your AI assistant (it needs to be able to run commands on your computer):

 Please read and then help me install my Switch game on my iPhone.

It moves forward with a few commands, and you can watch every step in the launcher window:

 

Anything only you can do (system permission prompts, signing in with your Apple ID, tapping Trust on your phone), the AI stops and asks you to do. On Windows, use s2armctl.cmd in the launcher folder with the same commands. Windows builds iPhone / iPad packages only, so for problems inside a game export the diagnostic bundle on the phone: long-press the game screen with four fingers for 1.5 seconds and choose Export diagnostics.

 Something wrong inside a game (graphics, frame rate, stutter, crashes)? Send your AI:

 Please read . My S2Arm game has this problem: . Check the settings first, then collect diagnostics; if you can change code, fix it at the root and open a PR, otherwise help me file an issue.

 Tested at scale

 211 games surveyed with a 95% first-try build success rate. 4,700+ test runs on real iOS devices and 1,000+ on macOS. Evidence

 Fast, smooth, and easy on the battery

On a 16 GB MacBook Air (M3), from importing a game to a finished iPhone build, completely cold:

 Game Game files Shaders Build time 
 --- --- --- --- 
 A 23.5 GB action RPG 23.5 GB 1,222 6.4 min 
 A 12.0 GB life-sim game 12.0 GB 9,315 8.6 min 
 A 17.5 GB open-world game 17.5 GB 26,999 34 min 

A Switch 2 game, measured on an iPhone 17 Pro Max: a full 60 fps while the phone is cool, 37–43 fps once sustained load has heated it up, at about 0.15 J per frame . Evidence

 Platforms

 Platform Support 
 --- --- 
 iPhone / iPad iOS / iPadOS 18 and later; every game is chosen inside one app 
 Mac Apple silicon, macOS 15 and later; builds locally and plays games right on the Mac 
 Windows Graphical launcher that builds and installs games for iPhone / iPad 
 Android / HarmonyOS Coming soon 

Evidence

 Downstream deep ports

Some games have a deep port made specially by the community. S2Arm recognizes these games: on export it shows a page explaining the option, and you can switch to the downstream project's route (importing, packing and installing are still buttons in S2Arm, with the downstream project's implementation underneath) or keep the standard route. The registry is pack/downstream/schemes.json ; the contract between the two is the downstream project's document.

 Route Project Devices Contract 
 --- --- --- --- 
 D2R-Mobile jhaizhou-ops/d2r-mobile iPhone / iPad (iOS 26 and later; Android and HarmonyOS in progress) docs/S2ARM.md 

 Getting started

1. Download the Mac or Windows launcher from the download page and open it. Building for iPhone on a Mac needs the free Xcode from the App Store, signed in with your Apple ID; the launcher walks you through it.
2. Import your own keys and games. Put the base game, updates and DLC in one folder and import them together.
3. Choose iPhone / iPad or this Mac, then click Build.
4. Follow the launcher to sign and install with your own Apple ID (the Windows launcher ships with the Impactor signing tool), open S2Arm, and pick a game from the library.

Back up your saves before updating the app. The release uses the new app identifier io.s2arm. , which the system treats as a new app: saves from the beta builds do not carry over automatically.

 Honest boundaries

S2Arm runs 64-bit (AArch64) games. Apple silicon cannot execute 32-bit ARM code, so 32-bit games are outside what S2Arm supports, as are games that need a 36-bit a
